reviews.text: A majority of the questions ask about when you wake up and whether it’s naturally or by an alarm, none of them take into consideration a parent who’s woken up by their child every day. So I don’t wake naturally, I suppose you could consider my kid an alarm but not really. None of the questions have any option to add being woken up by a child or being dictated by your children’s sleep schedule/wake-ups. So for that reason I feel like I can’t use this app. I’m not able to just sleep until my “wake window,” and I genuinely have no clue when my kid will wake up in the morning (could be 5:45, could be 7:30). Very frustrating since so many people have poor sleep like I do because of their kids.

In my case, I’m not the only one who uses the device, and even though I tell the AI that the data isn’t correct it won’t let me change it. Rise put me in a sleep schedule that only gives me 5 hours of sleep a night when it says I need 8:15. Asking me to go to bed 3 hours later than I do currently and getting up at the same time.

If you have a device that tracks your sleep accurately, then maybe this would work. If not, then I wouldn’t trust it.

reviews.text:
I really do like the concept of this app, but it has one major bug - it does not respect “do not disturb” settings on my phone. There’s been multiple times now when I went to bed early and turned my phone on do not disturb, only to be woken up by the Rise alert to start getting ready for bed. By not respecting the DND setting and waking me up, this is totally counterintuitive to the point of the app!

I emailed support about this, and their response was telling me to turn off alerts, completely avoiding the part about how it does not respect the DND setting. When I replied to them and once again pointed this out, I got no reply. 

FIX THIS BUG AND STOP WAKING PEOPLE UP WITH ALERTS WHEN DO NO DISTURB IS SET

reviews.title: Bugs Galore, Not That Great
reviews.text:
Not the app I hoped it would be. While the sheep debit number is a bit useful and the guidance section taught me it reminded me of a free things, the app is so full of bugs it’s ridiculous. 

For example there is a two hour difference between the “morning peak” the Home tab and the Energy tab tell me. With an I supposed to believe?

Additionally I switched most of my notifications to “text” instead of app notifications, which seems like a great and unique system if you hate  notifications like me, but bugs galore again, I’m still getting notifications IN ADDITION to the text messages, so there’s no way to stop them, I already set the settings to how I wanted them!

Also they have a complicated and annoying system if you want to fill out a bug report.

Finally I had hoped it would actually *actively coach* you and set a day by day schedule for you to slowly shift your sleep to a more work-appropriate time, but no, app is recommending I go to be at 1AM to “match” my melatonin window. I don’t want to MATCH it you dinguses, I want to MOVE it!

Really feels like false advertising on that last one. Even without bugs I would be disappointed, it’s not just what they claimed to advertise in the App Store/setup phase.

I guess I’ll give it another week since there are a few things I like (such as the reminder to stop looking at screens/put on orange glasses), but I am planning to ask for the full-refund-within-your-first-month.

It’s not at all worth $70.

reviews.title: I expected a lot more
reviews.text: Due to the advertisements I expected more. (“RISE suggested I wake up at 4 am to help with my puffy face”) and it doesn’t suggest anything- it tracks. They have a quiz for new customers that I wish they had for current users. The quiz is really cool but to get your results you have to sign up/pay right there (I already have an account and the quizzes are on Facebook advertisements) so why can’t a paying customer do the same quizzes to get the same insights and answers that a new person would receive? Plus once you actually buy it, the data is overwhelming- lots of charts and trends and tracking, but still no “advice” or “suggestions” to a better routine as advertised. Or maybe it does do that somewhere but it’s so confusing that I haven’t figured it out. They need some tutorial classes for this thing. It’s not easy to navigate at first. My biggest issue with it is that I deeply struggle with insomnia- but there’s only “awake” and “asleep” and once I input that I was “awake” from 4 am to 7am (insomnia- trying to sleep but failing) it reads this as “awake” and up and about so then my patterns are off- like it was saying that I was past my grogginess phase, past my morning energy spike and then into my first daily dip, as if I’d been awake and up and living life that entire time. Awake does not mean out of bed. And the 7am to 12pm nap? That was me catching up on sleep. Finally falling asleep after tossing and turning all night, but it didn’t get that data right. They really really need an insomnia function. Awake but trying to sleep- groggy until I fall back asleep. It’s just not matching up to what I expected and the data isn’t really all that accurate- maybe if you had an Apple Watch to sync to, that would be better but I don’t have one. It’s a little too complex imo and confusing. It has not helped me become a morning person- which has been my goal for a LONG time and the hardest thing I struggle with so that’s the reason I paid for it. If it’s because I’m not using it right then maybe they should have tutorials or people available to help walk you through it so that you can get the most out of it but I haven’t seen that at all.
